chapter: Capitol Records and "On the Street Where You Live"
title: Making Muted Jazz and the shuffle-beat "On the Street Where You Live"
summary: With George Rhodes's arrangements, Dave Cavanaugh asked for the last twenty minutes to be filled with "On the Street Where You Live" played in a shuffle beat; Jones and the band did it from the melody.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Oh, yeah. Sure. And it had a good sound. And they said, "Now, we're going to make one, make an album with you. We're going to call it Muted Jazz." Now, we play everything, all the things, the little arrangements, like, "Too Close for Comfort." A nice arrangement we had on there. Now we've got George Rhodes by this time. We've got George Rhodes. The other piano player, he thinks he's doing me a favor. I'm paying him the scale, but he says that, "I ain't going to help nobody build no band. That's all I did all my life, help people build bands. I ain't helping nobody else to build no band," you know. So I said, "Well, okay, whatever you think, you know. I'm giving you the scale. That's what they're paying me." So now we go down there and make all our stuff, arrangements that George Rhodes had. He wasn't working then, so he come on down with us. I found him and he come on down with us. And he said yes. So he started making little arrangements. "Too Close for Comfort." "The Man With the Golden Arm," and things like that. He had some nice little ideas, you know, to let you know the group was together, you know. It was limited with four pieces, but he played things that you knew -- make you know that the group was together, it wasn't a pickup group. And we played all our things, which we thought was great. So we had about 20 minutes to go on the album, Muted Jazz, and Dave said, "You know what I'd like to do? You've got about 20 minutes, Jonah." I said, "What?" He said,

"On the Street Where You Live." I said, "Oh, Dave, we don't know that thing." He said, "Well, I heard you do it in the club." I said, "We only do that when somebody asks for it. We just play the melody." He said, "Well, that's all I want you to do, play the melody. Play it through once and come back and play it an octave higher the second time, start from the last half." And he says, "Give it a shuffle beat." And he told the drummer just what kind of shuffle he wanted, because I had never played with a shuffle beat, so I couldn't tell him. So he said, "I want you to accent it, chunk, chunk, like that, you know." And he says, "Get an introduction." So Buster was around too, you know. He was always around me, you know. So he says, "Get a hit introduction." So Buster says, you do, (Singing). The piano goes (Singing). And again, (Singing). We played that thing and we got it through in time, in the 20 minutes or less, you know. And no, I don't know. We're up in Canada now, in London, Ontario. I forget the name of that -- Campbell's, in London, Ontario, and we used to go there every year. So while we're up there some people come in one night and say, "Jonah, why don't you play your record hit?" I said, "What's the name of it?" So she said, "What's that, On the Street Where You're Living, or something like that." I said, "Yeah?" She said, "Yeah, that's all they're playing around Cleveland and Detroit.
